component.name: SRS System Information
component.summary: Show what is inside your PC and whether it is healthy

description.p: SRS is a system information viewer for Linux. It shows the processor, memory, motherboard and BIOS, graphics and audio, drives, network, sensors, USB and PCI devices and the operating system, in plain words first and with every detail one click away.

The Overview answers "Is my PC OK?": temperatures judged against each sensor's own limit, drive health (SMART), hardware errors, free disk space and memory in use, each with a status light and an explanation.

SRS is inspired by SIV (System Information Viewer) by Ray Hinchliffe, RH Software. It is an independent project, not affiliated with SIV or its author, and contains no SIV code or data. A classic view with SIV-style windows is included.

ul.li: CPU and GPU burn-in and stress tests; Dhrystone, Whetstone, Cache & Memory, Storage, OS Latency, CPU Compute, Everyday Work, Network, GPU, GPU Compute comparison (Vulkan, ROCm/HIP, CUDA, OpenCL), SRS Pi, Crypto and Prime Sieve benchmarks and a memory latency test
Power & cost: an estimate of the whole PC's power use and its cost, with recorded history (estimates, not a meter reading)
Tabs you can arrange and save as lineups, sortable tables and a startup manager
Device ID lookup for PCI and USB devices
Reports saved as text, and a command-line report search
Optional root-only details (DMI, memory SPD, SMART, MSRs) collected with one password prompt
A built-in user guide: F1 opens it at the section for the item you are looking at

description.p: A Power & cost page that estimates the whole PC's power use and what it costs, with history, sessions, alarms and offline price tables. New benchmarks: Cache & Memory, Storage, OS Latency, CPU Compute, Everyday Work, Network, GPU Benchmark, GPU Burnin, GPU Compute comparison, SRS Pi, Crypto and Prime Sieve, with a run history; each asks before it starts. Tabs you can arrange and save as lineups, sortable tables, a Startup manager that turns startup items off and on without deleting anything, a Full access / Limited badge, and stock-versus-in-effect clocks on CPU Clocks.
Tested on one PC (Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT, wired connection): parts that need other hardware may have a bug or two. Please report them on GitHub Issues.

A new main window with an Overview that answers "Is my PC OK?", one page per category, search, and an AppImage for any distribution that can update itself. The classic SIV-style windows are still available.
